title: Auditing Published STR Allele Frequencies: A Reproducible Pipeline for Count Reconstruction and Regional Comparison in Colombia
content: Published short tandem repeat (STR) allele frequencies are often rounded, yet pooling samples requires allele counts. We developed an exact method that determines whether the reported frequencies and the number of typed allele copies admit one, several or no integer count vectors. We evaluated the method using genotypes from 617 Colombian individuals at 15 loci. When frequencies calculated from these genotypes were rounded to three decimal places, conventional reconstruction returned incorrect counts at 12 loci. The joint method recovered the exact counts at 4 loci and identified multiple compatible vectors at the remaining 11. In a separate comparison using the four-decimal frequency table published with the genotypes, three of six unique reconstructions matched the observed counts. Across 149 sample–locus distributions from 16 Colombian samples, 107 had a unique reconstruction, 1 was ambiguous and 41 were incompatible under the primary assumptions. Of the 107 distributions with a unique reconstruction, 71 met the inclusion criteria for regional analysis. Hudson’s FST between the Andean samples and the Chocó sample was 0.021. Across the eight loci used for simulation, the median Andean contribution to the pooled reference was 81% of allele copies. For simulated Chocó profiles, the ratio of the estimated random match probability under the Chocó reference to that under the pooled reference had a median of 5.0 at θ=0. At θ=0.01, this ratio exceeded ten for 24.63% of profiles. The pipeline supports the auditing of published reference tables. Its use in forensic casework requires separate validation.
